items: 21. May be the HEART OF GAIA: in the sense of being that which originated and now maintains, protects, directs, and/or evolves the life-favorable elements and phenomena of the geos [geological, hydrological, and atmospheric].

22. LIFE may mainly or simultaneously be EVOLVING BACKWARDS TOWARD SIMPLICITY OR THE TINIEST forms of matter, or may be predominantly evolving around the eschatological and archological 'black hole' or 'essential singularity' of the genome or chromosomes.

23. FOR BEING THE SIMPLEST organisms or the organisms with the fewest parts or least cumbersome and interfering genomes [or, more esoterically, for being that which is closest to the paradoxically and mysteriously preinfinite and supertemporal apeiron]: MAY BE THE MOST EVOLVED, in general or in special and key ways.
24. May actually have EVOLVED LARGER ORGANISMS: to serve as useful servants, vehicles, tools, habitats, or experiments.

25. It is NOT NECESSARILY true that the smallest organisms--or at least, neontological forms of same--are the MOST ANCIENT or least derivative; larger organisms, or what we call higher organisms, may have come earlier and given rise to at least those tiniest organisms we see around us today, or the latter may be utterly transformed versions or mimics of what were in fact the earliest, most primitive, lowest, or tiniest organisms.

26. 'LARGENESS' OR MULTICELLULARITY--against the near-infinity of other and orthogonal biological dimensions--may be a relatively superficial and even IRRELEVANT trait that is merely conspicuous or anthropocentric; the presently or ultimately most advanced or important evolutionary directions, vectors, or goals may be unrelated, dimensionless, merely additive, or synthetic and even 'holonomical': with respect to size, mass, redundancy (meristic or auxetic), complexity, longevity, or the like.
27. SIMILARLY [vide #26] FOR OTHER ANTHROPOMORPHOUS DIMENSIONS and qualities: not excepting even intelligence or civilization [at least as we ourselves know or are conscious of them].
28. Evolution's thrust and accomplishment may essentially be bipolar and antisyzygial: with LIFE AT ITS SMALLEST as important as, and complementary or even COESSENTIAL TO, LIFE AT ITS BIGGEST.

29. EVOLUTION may be BIPOLAR [or have two competing, separate, orthogonal, parallel, convergent, divergent, vergent, or adjoint themes] in another sense [cf. #28], esp. IN THE SENSE OF 'LINEAL VS. CROSS-LINEAL GENE FLOW': where macroorganisms may dominate or rely mainly on one ('lineal' evolution, say), and microbes, the other; and this might mean that microbes are the 'lower' form of life in the one sense, the higher form in the other sense.

30. Human BIOLOGISTS' PERCEPTION of microbes may be astonishingly BLINKERED by ANTHROPOMORPHIC, or at least anthropological, percepts and concepts, and per se largely unable to see--at all, fairly, or easily--the related or alien phenes and genetic factors that are peculiar or essential to microbes and to their ultimate evolutionary comparison with man or other macroorganisms: incl. the XENOMORPHIC organelles, growth processes, dynamics, evolutionary and taxonomic characters, needs, products, mutual and hierarchical interactions, ecological life, powers, phenomena, and other fundamentums and nuances.
31. It might be that MOST OF THE earth's BIOMASS and/or cells are microbial.

32. It is theoretically possible that microbes, in the subsequent course of evolution, progressively and more or less comprehensively SUBSUME [copy, emulate, or 'analogically equal'] or reevolve within themselves the diverse evolutionary INNOVATIONS--be they morphological or physiological--THAT FIRST APPEAR ON the MACROORGANISMAL LEVEL.

33. Since for present-day biology the overall or basic DIRECTION of biological evolution, ESSENCE OF LIFE, intrinsic complexity of life, and fundamental and holistic laws of life are all UNKNOWN: it really makes very little sense for us to speak--even tentatively--of one organism as 'higher' and another as 'lower'.
34. We already know of MANY WAYS [anatomical, physiological, etc] in which microbes are definitely much MORE ADVANCED than--or excel--larger and so-called 'higher' organisms.

35. Some novel and clearly REVOLUTIONARY BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS and phenomena MAY EXIST IN microbes that evidently have yet to be independently evolved in, or transferred to, larger and supposedly higher--or highest--organisms.

36. NATURE'S LITTLEST ENTITIES, phenomena, or events are paradoxically very OFTEN THE MOST IMPORTANT ones acting in the context of the largest ones--or the totality of things--as [literal or metaphoric]: catalysts, triggers, critical breaks, critical intermediaries, gadflies, organizers, pathbreakers, starters, spokesmen, governmental representatives, tools, wheels, lattice point-defects or slip planes, ions, free radicals, Josephson effects, etc.
